prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Atlanta for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” dentist for implants in Atlanta—“best” depends on your case (single implant vs full-arch), preferences (comfort with sedation, price, esthetics), and how complex your needs are (bone grafting, sinus lift, immediate load). I can help you find a top provider, but first here are practical guidelines so you can pick the right clinician for your situation.

Who to see
- For straightforward single-tooth implants: a periodontist or oral & maxillofacial surgeon (OMFS) usually places the implant; a restorative dentist or prosthodontist does the crown.
- For complex reconstructions, full-arch or severe bone loss: look for an OMFS, periodontist, or prosthodontist with specific implant reconstruction experience.
- Prosthodontists specialize in the restoration (crowns/bridges/dentures) and are helpful when esthetics and long-term function matter.

Important credentials and experience
- Specialty training: periodontist, OMFS, or prosthodontist.
- Board certification or fellowship (e.g., Diplomate of the American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, American Board of Periodontology, AAID credentials).
- Years and number of implants placed and success rates.
- Experience with the specific procedure you need (sinus lifts, bone grafting, immediate-loading implants, All-on-4).
- Use of modern tech: CBCT (3D imaging), guided implant surgery, digital planning, intraoral scanners.

What to ask at a consult
- How many implants have you placed and what is your success rate?
- Will you use CBCT and guided planning for my case?
- Who will place the implant and who will make the crown/prosthesis?
- What implant system/brand do you use and why?
- Do you do the bone grafting/sinus lift if needed? What are the alternatives?
- Sedation options and associated costs.
- Total cost estimate (implant body, abutment, crown, grafts, extractions) and financing.
- Warranty/guarantee and policy for complications or failures.
- Can I see before/after photos and patient references?

Practical tips for choosing
- Get referrals from your general dentist and from friends/family.
- Check professional directories: American Academy of Implant Dentistry (AAID), American Academy of Periodontology, or state dental society.
- Read reviews (Google, Healthgrades, RealSelf) but weigh clinical credentials more heavily than ratings alone.
- Meet for a consultation — most offer one — and choose the clinician who explains the plan clearly and answers your questions.

Costs and timeline (ballpark)
- Single implant (implant + abutment + crown): commonly $2,500–$6,000 total in the U.S. (varies by location and complexity).
- Add $300–$3,000+ for bone grafts/sinus lifts if needed.
- Timeline: 3–6 months typical from placement to final crown for conventional healing; immediate-load options may shorten this but aren’t appropriate for all cases.

Would you like me to:
- Find and shortlist highly rated implant specialists in Atlanta (I can search online for current providers), or
- Help you evaluate 2–3 specific dentists you already have in mind?

Tell me whether you want only oral surgeons/periodontists or also prosthodontists, any location preference (zip code or neighborhood), and whether budget or insurance matters, and I’ll prepare a shortlist.
